articles.title: Your Dashboard Says "Live" — Prove It With Freshness Watermarks
articles.excerpt: I once shipped a monitoring page that said LIVE in confident green letters. It stayed green for eleven days while the ingest job behind it had been dead for nine of them. The label was a CSS class. It…
articles.body: I once shipped a monitoring page that said LIVE in confident green letters. It stayed green for eleven days while the ingest job behind it had been dead for nine of them. The label was a CSS class. It had never once looked at the data. That was the week I stopped treating freshness as a display feature and started treating it as a data property — something each row carries, something every query can be tested against, something that fails loudly. This post is the pattern I use now: freshness watermarks. The label is a claim; the row is the evidence A dashboard badge claims "the view you're seeing is current." The only evidence for that claim lives in the data itself: when was this record last observed?
articles.author: Yuhe He

articles.title: Beyond Transcripts: Building an AI-Powered Empathy Engine for Mental Health
articles.excerpt: In the world of mental health counseling, the "magic" happens in the nuances—the pauses, the shifts in tone, and the emotional resonance between the therapist and the client. However, capturing these…
articles.body: In the world of mental health counseling, the "magic" happens in the nuances—the pauses, the shifts in tone, and the emotional resonance between the therapist and the client. However, capturing these moments for clinical supervision or progress tracking is notoriously difficult. Traditionally, therapists rely on manual notes, which are prone to bias and often miss the subtle flow of real-time transcription and sentiment analysis . Today, we are building a sophisticated Audio Intelligence pipeline. By combining Voice Activity Detection (VAD) , lightning-fast transcription, and Large Language Models (LLMs), we can transform raw audio into a structured map of human connection.

articles.body: On 13 October 2026, Pixalate shipped Ad Fraud API 3.0 with named invalid-traffic reason codes, including SSAI Misrepresentation for requests that claim server-side insertion but fail metadata checks. That is progress on the bid object. It is not proof that the VAST the stitcher pulls next carries playable media. Court TV and other publishers are rolling out Yospace-style SSAI while buyers still QA tags with XSD and a green dashboard. The gap between those two checks is where CTV revenue quietly disappears. Creative readiness means the tag matches the environment that was bought: SSAI transcode paths, HTTPS-only players, pod clocks, and identity fields on the deal. A document can validate and still never serve.

articles.body: My cybersecurity course teaches threat modelling with Microsoft's Threat Modeling Tool (TMT). You draw a data-flow diagram of a system, and TMT generates a list of STRIDE threats from rules in a template, then you triage each one. There was one problem: TMT only runs on Windows. I'm on a 2019 Intel MacBook Pro that already struggles, and running Windows in a virtual machine on it was not going to happen. So I built ThreatSketch : TMT's threat generation, from TMT's own template, in an app that runs in the browser, on macOS, on Windows and on Linux. Here's how it got there, including the version I threw away. What already existed Two tools sat on either side of the gap: Microsoft TMT generates threats automatically.

articles.body: Apple has finally announced its long-rumored foldable: the iPhone Duo . The new phone has a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display, a “nano‑texture” finish on the inner screen, and barely any visible crease. Instead of Face ID, it uses Touch ID on the power button. It has two cameras, a main lens and a wide-angle lens. Apple completely revamped iOS 27’s controls and apps for the foldable, including putting the dock on the side of the phone. And it has a flashy opening animation when you unfold the phone. The iPhone Duo a big new bet from Apple, though one that’s a little late to the game compared to competitors like Samsung and Google. The phone isn’t cheap: it starts at $1,999 for the base 256GB model, and the prices only go up from there.

articles.excerpt: The astronauts of SpaceX's Crew-12 mission wish that we could all see Earth as they just did —as a beautiful but fragile outpost of life in a vast void.
articles.body: The astronauts of SpaceX's Crew-12 mission to the International Space Station wish that we could all see Earth as they just did. An orbital view reveals the immense beauty of our blue planet, the only world we know of that hosts life. But it also highlights how fragile that life is, tethered to our lonely Earth in the vast void of space, according to Crew-12 commander Jessica Meir of NASA. "You see this very thin, tenuous band of an atmosphere , and you know that that is all that is supporting life, and we really need to do our best to protect it," Meir said on Thursday afternoon (Oct. 15), during a press conference that discussed the recently concluded Crew-12 mission .

articles.body: I used to think being interested in the night sky meant I had to try every meteor shower. If a calendar said "peak," I interpreted that as an instruction. I'd set an alarm, find several layers of clothing and go outside at around 2:00 a.m. when even the neighborhood cats seemed surprised to see me. Then I'd spend an increasingly resentful 45 minutes staring upward, occasionally see one meteor and wonder whether I was somehow doing it all wrong. As I've grown into stargazing, I've become much more selective. The Orionids peak next week, and normally I'd be tempted. These fast meteors come from debris from Halley's Comet , which is enough of a connection to make almost anyone want to go outside.

articles.title: Scientists find 'gemstones' in atmosphere of bizarre, scorching-hot 'marshmallow' exoplanet
articles.excerpt: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers have unravelled some of the secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot exoplanet that has the consistency of marshmallow.
articles.body: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have unraveled some of the atmospheric secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot world that has the consistency of marshmallow. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , under the watchful infrared eye of the JWST , is WASP-17b, located around 1,300 light-years away. The exoplanet has a mass around 0.8 times that of Jupiter, but it is around twice as wide as the solar system's largest planet, giving it a "super-puff" consistency comparable to the Earth-based treat. WASP-17 b is so close to its parent star that it completes an orbit in under four Earth days, with this proximity also making the temperature of this " hot Jupiter " skyrocket.

articles.title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower 2026 peak this week — and when to look
articles.excerpt: The Orionids peak around Oct. 21. Here's when and where to look for the best chance of spotting meteors.
articles.body: If you love watching meteors, 2026 has given you plenty to enjoy. This summer, the annual Perseid meteor shower peaked on the day of a new moon — and a solar eclipse — so moonlight stayed out of the way. And there's more to look forward to: in December, the Geminids, the year's most prolific shower, will peak after a waxing crescent moon sets early in the evening, opening the door to excellent viewing. Right between those two headline showers, the dependable Orionids take their turn, reaching peak activity around Oct. 21-22. So, when and where can you catch the show? When and where to watch Make sure you wrap up warm for a night of Orionid hunting.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 16, 1975: NASA launches the 1st-ever GOES weather satellite to watch Earth from space
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 16, 1975, NASA launched the first operational GOES weather satellite. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 16, 1975, NASA launched the first operational GOES satellite! GOES-A was the first in a series of weather satellites that NASA jointly operated with the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). The name is short for Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite . GOES-A launched on a Delta rocket from Cape Canaveral, Florida. GOES satellites all have a geostationary orbit, which means they always face the same part of Earth — in this case, the Indian Ocean. Once GOES-A became operational, it was renamed GOES-1. The GOES satellite fleet has grown over the years, and is a critical link in the chain of satellites tracking Earth's weather from space.
